title: RSE 7/12: Solar eclipse global search (swe_sol_eclipse_when_glob)
description:
### Summary
Port `swe_sol_eclipse_when_glob`: find the next/previous solar eclipse anywhere on Earth from `tjd_start`, with full contact-time array and eclipse-type classification. Exposes `Ephemeris::sol_eclipse_when_glob` (`&self`).

Depends on **RSE 5** (`eclipse_where`, `calc_planet_star`, types) and **RSE 3** (`find_maximum`/`find_zero` in `math.rs`).

### Files
- `src/eclipse.rs` — add `SolarEclipseGlobal` result struct, `sol_eclipse_when_glob`.
- `src/context.rs` — `pub fn sol_eclipse_when_glob(&self, tjd_start, ifl: CalcFlags, ifltype: EclipseFlags, backward: bool) -> Result<SolarEclipseGlobal, Error>`.
- `src/lib.rs` — re-export `SolarEclipseGlobal`.
- `tests/c-gen/gen_eclipse.c` — add key `sol_when_glob`; regenerate `eclipse.json`.
- `tests/golden/eclipse.rs` — add `#[test] sol_when_glob`.

### Implementation steps
Read `docs/c-ref-eclipse-solar.md` §5.1–§5.9 and §7 (parabola helpers, already ported to `math.rs` in RSE 3).

1. **`SolarEclipseGlobal`**: fields = `tret[0..10]` per §5.8 (maximum, `tret[1]`=RA-conjunction/local-noon instant, C1..C4 contact times, centre-line begin/end, ...) + the returned type bitmask. Name fields exactly per §5.8 (flag §5.8 as the GLOBAL-search semantics — different from local, RSE 8).
2. **`sol_eclipse_when_glob`** (§5): 
   - `ifltype` validation/normalisation (§5.1).
   - Lunation stepping (§5.2): Meeus synodic-month step using the K/T argument (constants in §5.2); the F-argument (Moon argument of latitude) filter eliminating ~70% of new moons (threshold in §5.2).
   - Iterative refinement to minimum Sun–Moon separation via `find_maximum` (§5.3).
   - Confirm & classify total/annular/partial (§5.4), calling `eclipse_where` at the max instant.
   - Contact-time refinement C1..C4 (§5.5) via `find_zero`.
   - Annular-total (hybrid) detection (§5.6).
   - `tret[1]` RA-conjunction instant (§5.7).
   - Return the eclipse-type bitmask (§5.9).
   - `backward` flips the stepping direction.

### C reference
`docs/c-ref-eclipse-solar.md` §5 (all subsections), §7, §0.

### Golden tests
- **C harness** add key `sol_when_glob`: for `tjd_start ∈ {2451545.0 /*2000*/, 2459000.5 /*2020*/}`, `backward ∈ {0,1}`, `ifltype ∈ {0 /*all types*/}`, call `swe_sol_eclipse_when_glob(tjd_start, SEFLG_MOSEPH, ifltype, tret, backward, serr)`. Emit `{tjd_start, backward, retval, tret:[0..10]}`. Regenerate `eclipse.json`.
- **Rust test** `#[test] sol_when_glob`: assert `tret[0..10]` via `assert_f64_eps(.., 1e-5)` (≈1 s on contact instants); assert returned flags == `retval`.
- `cargo test --test golden eclipse::sol_when_glob -- --nocapture` passes.

### Acceptance criteria
- `cargo build` + `cargo clippy --all-targets` clean.
- `cargo test --test golden eclipse::sol_when_glob -- --nocapture` passes (1e-5 day).

### Escape hatch
If contact times fail > 1e-4 day after two attempts, STOP and report failing `(tjd_start, backward)` + which `tret[]` slot diverges + the eclipse type mismatch if any. Read `swecl.c:1185–1515` directly. Escalate to Opus after two attempts.

acceptance_criteria.text: cargo test --test golden eclipse::sol_when_glob -- --nocapture passes (1e-5 day)

execution_record: Straightforward 1:1 port; all 4 golden cases passed on first attempt (no debugging session needed). One deliberate deviation from C, documented inline and in codebase-map.md: C's find_zero (swecl.c:4148) can return ERR on a negative discriminant, but swe_sol_eclipse_when_glob's caller ignores that return value and leaves dt1/dt2 (and hence tret[i1]/tret[i2]) at whatever stale value they held from a previous find_zero call or their zero-initialized declaration. Rust's find_maximum/find_zero (math.rs) return Option and there's no natural "stale global" to carry forward statelessly, so on None we leave tret[i1]/tret[i2] at 0.0 (matching C's actual first-ever-call behavior, just not its cross-call staleness). This is unreachable for well-conditioned real eclipses (the contact-time parabolas always have real roots) and was flagged rather than silently diverged from.

messages.author: agent
messages.text: Review: approve with notes. sol_eclipse_when_glob verified against swecl.c:1185-1515 — the duplicated d>180 reduction and signed a<1e-10 break are literal C quirks (confirmed in source), contact_dc cross-quirk (penumbra/cos_umbra) matches, hybrid detection + type filters + 3-pass ET→UT all exact. One note: on find_zero()→None the Rust leaves tret[i1]/tret[i2]=0.0 and skips refinement, while C assigns tjd+dta (zero-init dt1/dt2) and refines anyway; the code comment mischaracterizes C ("leaves tret at whatever they held before"). Practically unreachable for real eclipses; fix the comment at minimum.
